title: Escalation Scripting and Evidence Checklist for New Responders
author: Maya Kapoor
content:
Overview
--------
This document is a prescriptive operator playbook for escalation scripting and evidence collection aimed at new responders joining on-call rotations. It contains:
- a compact decision ladder for severity and escalation,
- an evidence checklist to collect reproducible artifacts,
- operator-to-operator escalation scripts and templates,
- customer status page / CSR templates for rapid publication, and
- runbook quality gates used by SRE leads to approve runbooks used in rotations.

Scope
-----
Applies to: production-facing services and infra that can cause customer-visible degradations. Primary service examples in scope: redwood-serving-api, routing-proxy, kv-cache, console-frontend, embeddings-service.
Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (follow maintenance playbook), purely experimental canary jobs (follow canary runbook).

Severity definitions (decision ladder)
-----------------------------------
1) Sev-1 (Critical): full outage or data-loss affecting >20% of active requests or any customer SLA breach (99.9% availability target missed for 15+ minutes).
2) Sev-2 (High): significant feature loss or severe degradation producing >5% error rate or p95 latency >2x SLO across a region for 15+ minutes.
3) Sev-3 (Medium): intermittent errors or latency spikes localized to subset of customers / regions with mitigation available.
4) Sev-4 (Low): informational, non-customer impacting issues, operational tasks.

SLO quick reference (for escalation thresholds)
- redwood-serving-api: availability 99.95% (monthly), p95 latency <200ms, error rate <0.15%
- embeddings-service: availability 99.9%, p95 latency <500ms, error rate <0.5%
- kv-cache: eviction rate <0.02 ops/sec per node; sustained evictions >5m triggers Sev-2

Immediate operator checklist (first 10 minutes)
----------------------------------------------
1) Acknowledge page in PagerDuty / incident system and claim incident channel (Slack #incident-[id]).
2) Set initial status: severity estimate, initial impact statement, and bridge link. Example: "Sev-2: Increased 5xx on redwood-serving-api (US-EAST). Bridge: https://zoom/bridge/123"
3) Run triage probes (below).
4) Start evidence collection (persist artifacts to incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/YYYYMMDD-[id]/).
5) If uncertain on scope, escalate to oncall@engineering after 10 minutes with evidence.

Triage probes (quick commands)
- Check ingestion and routing: curl -sS https://metrics.internal/api/health | jq .
- Query latency and errors (last 10m):
  - grafana query: service="redwood-serving-api" AND region="us-east-1" | p95, error_rate
- Check downstream dependencies: kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=kv-cache -o wide
- Check recent deploys: gcloud builds list --filter="status=SUCCESS" --limit=5 --project=redwood-prod

Evidence collection checklist (required artifacts)
------------------------------------------------
Collect and upload the following artifacts into the incident evidence folder. Each artifact below is required for Sev-1/Sev-2; optional for Sev-3/Sev-4.

| Artifact | How to capture | Retention label (s3 path) | Notes |
|---------|----------------|---------------------------|-------|
| Timeline of events | Incident timeline text file (timeline.txt) | s3://redwood-incidents/YYYYMMDD-[id]/timeline.txt | Include timestamps (UTC) and first-seen signals. |
| Primary error logs | redwood-serving-api stderr/stdout (last 60m) | s3://redwood-incidents/YYYYMMDD-[id]/logs/primary.log | clipped to relevant request IDs. |
| Request traces | Distributed traces for 5 failing requests | s3://redwood-incidents/YYYYMMDD-[id]/traces/trace-*.json | Include trace IDs referenced in postmortem. |
| Metrics snapshot | prometheus export (10m window) | s3://redwood-incidents/YYYYMMDD-[id]/metrics/snapshot.prom | Graphs exported as PNG optional. |
| Config/deploy diff | git diff --name-only HEAD...origin/main | s3://redwood-incidents/YYYYMMDD-[id]/deploy/diff.txt | Include any runtime flag or infra changes. |
| Core dumps / heap profiles | gcore/lldb profiles | s3://redwood-incidents/YYYYMMDD-[id]/profiles/* | Capture safely; scrub PII. |

Minimum evidence checklist (quick)
- timeline.txt (first 15m entry)
- primary.log (last 20m, clipped)
- metrics/snapshot.prom (10m window)
- trace samples (if tracing enabled)

Escalation script: operator-to-operator (voice/Slack)
---------------------------------------------------
Use plain, factual language. Keep message concise and include a call-to-action. Follow this script when escalating to second-line or oncall lead: 

Slack template (DM):
"Hi <Name>, I’m oncall for redwood-serving-api. We have a suspected Sev-2: error rate 6% in us-east-1 for 12m. Evidence: timeline + primary.log uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/20241102-1010/. Initial triage done: ruled out recent deploys, kv-cache eviction spike coincides. Can you take the bridge? I’ll put a short handoff message in #incident-bridge."

Voice/phone template:
- Identify: "Hi, this is <your name>, oncall for redwood-serving-api."
- State impact: "We are seeing ~6% 5xx rate in us-east, affecting customer traffic."
- Summarize evidence and actions taken (2–3 bullets).
- Ask for explicit role: "Can you accept bridge ownership and investigate storage layer?"

Bridging and role assignment
- Bridge owner coordinates work items and assigns: primary investigator, deploy ruler, comms lead, and customer liaison.
- Role table:
  - Bridge owner: retains single source of truth (incident doc header).
  - Primary investigator: deep-dive into service logs/traces.
  - Deploy ruler: verify and, if necessary, initiate rollback.
  - Comms lead: prepares status updates and customer templates.
  - Customer liaison: coordinates with CSMs for impacted accounts.

Status page and customer comms templates
--------------------------------------
Status page short (public) — first 15 minutes:
"Redwood Inference is investigating elevated error rates impacting text generation in US-EAST. Some requests may fail or be delayed. We will post updates here every 30 minutes."

Customer-facing email / CSR template (when impacted customers identified):
Subject: Incident affecting text-generation in US-EAST (Incident ID: IR-2024-XXXX)

Hi <Customer Name>,

We’re investigating an incident affecting text-generation requests in US-EAST. Some requests may receive 5xx responses or experience higher latency. Our oncall team has identified a suspected service interaction and is actively working on mitigation. We will follow up with a technical summary and ETA by <ETA time>.

If this incident is causing urgent business impact, reply to this message and we will prioritize your case.

- Redwood Inference Operations

Post-handoff validation checklist (when handing to next operator)
---------------------------------------------------------------
1) Confirm bridge owner and next oncall (explicit acceptance).
2) Ensure evidence folder contains the minimum checklist.
3) Confirm short-term mitigations applied and measurable impact (e.g., error rate down from 6% to 1%).
4) Record handoff time and responsible person in timeline.txt.

Runbook quality gates (for runbook approvers)
-------------------------------------------
Before a runbook is promoted to oncall rotation it must pass these gates: 
- Ownership section present with >=2 oncallable contacts.
- Minimum viable triage steps (first 10m) documented and validated in a tabletop.
- Evidence checklist section with required artifact capture commands.
- Tested in at least one game-day in the last 6 months.
- No hardcoded credentials or PII in snippets.

Approval process: reviewer performs a tabletop run with the author; results added to the runbook change note; SRE lead sets status="rotation-ready".

Game day mini-syllabus (for new responders)
-------------------------------------------
1) 60m orientation: incident decision ladder, severity criteria, and tools (PagerDuty, Slack incident channels, evidence bucket).
2) 90m guided simulation: synthetic error injected (kv-cache evictions) with scripted alerts.
3) 30m debrief: focus on evidence quality and communication templates.
4) 30m sign-off: new responder must gather and upload minimum evidence and lead a short 10-minute status update.

Evidence handling and privacy notes
----------------------------------
- Always scrub PII before uploading (use incident-scrub tool: scrubbify --path ./primary.log --remove-ips --remove-emails).
- Mark artifacts with confidentiality tag in S3 metadata (x-amz-meta-confidentiality=internal).
- For customer data exposures, involve security@redwood immediately and follow the data-exposure SOP.

Typical triage timeline (example)
--------------------------------
T+0:00 — page acknowledged; bridge and Slack channel created.
T+0:05 — initial triage complete; evidence folder started.
T+0:10 — escalate to oncall lead if impact >= Sev-2.
T+0:30 — customer-facing status posted and refreshed every 30m.
T+1:00 — mitigation applied or rollback initiated; continue monitoring.

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Primary owner: SRE rotation (oncall@engineering)
- Escalation faucet: oncall-lead@redwood.com
- Security escalation: security@redwood.com
- Incident artifact bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
-------------------------------------
Collect traces by trace ID (example):
curl -sS "https://traces.internal/api/trace/{{trace_id}}" -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TRACING_TOKEN' > trace-{{trace_id}}.json

Export a Prometheus snapshot for last 10 minutes (example):
# use promcurl or grafana backend
promcurl query_range --query='rate(http_requests_total[10m])' --start='10m' --end='now' --step=15s > snapshot.prom

Upload evidence folder:
aws s3 cp ./evidence s3://redwood-incidents/YYYYMMDD-[id]/ --recursive --acl bucket-owner-full-control

Appendix B: Glossary and links
- Bridge: the active coordination call (Zoom) for the incident.
- Evidence bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/
- Incident doc template: /confluence/templates/incident-doc-basic
- Runbook PR checklist: /confluence/eng-oncall/runbook-pr-checklist
